comments.text:
Once a video has been generated and viewed, the pixels have already left the building. You can delete the official copy from OpenAI’s servers, but you can’t claw back what’s already displayed on someone’s screen. A few key points:

Screen recording is trivial. Even if Sora 2 prevents direct downloads or embedding, any user can record their screen with native OS tools or third-party capture software.

Deletion only affects hosted content. When the likeness owner deletes a video, that removes it from OpenAI’s platform — but not from local or redistributed copies.

Off topic, but wanted to throw it out there. 

AI Defaulting to a Negative.

In a chat about Epistemic Conflict this is example the model chose to use:

“Experts disagree on the cause of the economic downturn.” 

Which led me to thinking,
- out of all possible examples, why did this get attention?
- why would it go for a double negative example?
- would it have been better if the model, in a neutral situation, to tend toward a positive rather than a negative?
- is negativity being reinforced inadvertently?
- is this the foundational core we want to be building on?

I get that it may seem trivial, but the cumulative effect over time would be significant.

I think it would be worth testing models for positive/negative aspect. 
Not so that behaviour is overtly positive, just so that in a 50/50 scenario, AI lean positive rather than negative.
